# Proposal: Cap host-floor inheritance for small-diff subagent calls

**Incident.** Across `portulan`, `portulan-internal`, and `acme-web`, memory entries recorded the same failure three times. Subagent calls inherited the 85k-token host floor (`F`) even when the work was a 50-line diff. Each small review or edit paid for the full host context, though it needed only a fraction of it.

**Proposed rule.** A subagent call whose input is a small diff must not inherit `F`. The caller passes the diff and the acceptance criteria. The subagent starts from a minimal context and gets more only on explicit request. The size threshold for "small" is open for review, and 50 lines is the observed case.

**Enforcement.** The delegation step checks the diff size before spawning a subagent. It blocks inheritance of `F` below the threshold and logs the token cost of each call. A verify recipe compares per-call token cost against `F` and fails if a small-diff call starts at or above it. The proposal does not yet say whether this check belongs in a hook or in the reviewer's checklist. That choice goes to the human gate.

**Provenance.** form=link, href=https://github.com/sleepy-panda-srl/portulan/pull/433. The three recurring memory entries in `portulan`, `portulan-internal`, and `acme-web` are consolidated here, and PR 433 is the cited source for the incident.

**Retire when.** The host stops imposing a fixed floor on subagent calls, or subagent context is scoped to the task by default. It also retires if the verify recipe shows no small-diff call starting near `F` for a full review cycle.

# Proposal: Lean context for small-diff subagent calls

**Incident.** In three repositories (`portulan`, `portulan-internal`, `acme-web`), memory entries recorded the same failure. Subagent calls inherited the host's 85k-token floor (`F`) even when the task was a 50-line diff. Each small review or edit paid for the full host context, which made it slow and costly and left less room for the work itself.

**Proposed rule.** Before delegating a task whose diff is small (about 50 lines or fewer), the delegating agent must give the subagent a minimal brief: the diff, the acceptance criteria, and the files to read. It must not let the subagent inherit the full host context. If a lean spawn isn't possible, it must say so in the handoff and record the actual starting token cost.

**Enforcement.** Add a check to the pre-commit and review handoff recipe. It compares the subagent's starting context against `F` for diffs under the small-diff threshold, and flags any call that starts at or near `F`. A flag is a warning for the first review cycle. It becomes a gate only after the human or eval gate has confirmed the threshold and the measurement method.

**Provenance.** [portulan#433](https://github.com/sleepy-panda-srl/portulan/pull/433) (`form=link`, `href=https://github.com/sleepy-panda-srl/portulan/pull/433`). It is corroborated by three recurring memory entries in `portulan`, `portulan-internal`, and `acme-web`.

**Retire when.** The host stops imposing the `F` floor on subagent calls, or subagents can be spawned with a context scoped to the task by default. Check this when the host or harness changes, and retire the rule once small-diff subagent calls start well below `F` without any manual briefing.
